description: Home-fitness equipment brand (walking pads, adjustable dumbbells, resistance gear) run by AURAVIA RESEARCH LTD, registered in England and Wales, selling across the EU, UK, Switzerland and Norway. Its own affiliate programme pays tiered commission with creator assets and free product for qualifying creators, and states there is no cap on commission.

evidence.summary: Official affiliate page: 20% commission on the first referred sale, 15% standard ongoing rate, and 20% again after EUR 2,000 in lifetime referred sales; 30-day cookie; monthly payouts by bank transfer or PayPal with a EUR 50 minimum.

Commission cap stated explicitly on the official page: 'No cap - On total commission - ever', and the FAQ answers 'Is there really no cap on commission?' with 'Correct - there's no ceiling built into the programme... no maximum payout.'

Programme is built for fitness creators and influencers: no follower minimum, no exclusivity, creator assets and early product access, free product for qualifying creators; contact email info@auraviafitness.com with the subject line 'affiliate'.

name: AuraVia Fitness

reasons.compensation: 15% standard rate (20% on the first sale and again after EUR 2,000 lifetime referred sales), with explicit no-cap wording in both the hero terms and the FAQ.
reasons.contact_access: Published affiliate email (info@auraviafitness.com) with subject-line guidance on the official page.
reasons.credibility: The page names a registered UK company (AURAVIA RESEARCH LTD, England and Wales) with a London address, but the brand is young and little-known, so credibility stays low.
reasons.niche_fit: Compact home-fitness gear (walking pads, adjustable dumbbells) is a natural demo and review fit for fitness and home-workout creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application on the brand's own page with no follower minimum.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Official page is explicitly built for fitness creators with assets, early access and free product, but publishes no creator counts, so the score stays mid-range.

description: Large US sports-nutrition and supplement store carrying 7,000+ products. Its long-running affiliate program is partnered with Commission Junction (CJ Affiliate) and pays a flat 10% commission on all referred orders, with no cap on earnings stated in its official FAQ.

evidence.summary: Official FAQ: 'We offer an excellent commission to our affiliates, with no caps on the amount you can earn! You'll earn a flat 10% commission all orders sent to us.'

Official page: the program is partnered with Commission Junction (CJ); affiliates promote a store of 7,000+ products across supplements, equipment, apparel and accessories; joining is free and affiliates get banners, text links and data feeds.
Eligibility limits on the official page: affiliates accepted worldwide except China and India and certain US nexus states (AR, CT, IL, NY, NC, RI); no cashback or loyalty sites.

name: Muscle & Strength

reasons.compensation: Flat 10% on all orders with an explicit no-cap statement in the official FAQ; a mid-range rate on a very large catalogue.
reasons.contact_access: No direct partnerships email is published on the page; contact runs through the CJ network application.
reasons.credibility: Long-established US supplement retailer running its program through CJ Affiliate, a major network.
reasons.niche_fit: One of the largest supplement catalogues in the niche (7,000+ products), so almost any fitness creator's audience products are covered.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free, open signup via CJ on the official page.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Runs through CJ with standard affiliate creative (banners, links, data feeds); the page does not publish creator counts or UGC-specific terms, so saturation stays unknown.

description: Worldwide campervan rental booking platform. Its own affiliate program pays a rising share of the net profit on every confirmed booking (30% rising to 50%), with ready-made links, banners, widgets, an embeddable search box and a live per-post analytics panel, and states there is no cap on earnings.

evidence.summary: Official FAQ: 'You start at 30% of our net profit per booking and rise to 50% as you drive more bookings. The more your content converts, the more you earn, with no cap.' Note the commission is a share of net profit, not of the booking price.

Toolkit for creators: deep links, banners, widgets, an embeddable search box and source-labelled links that show exactly which post brought each booking; links work on social media, newsletters and videos - no website required.
Published contact on the affiliate page: hello@campervanplanet.com, plus phone numbers for the US, New Zealand, Australia, the UK and Canada.

name: Campervan Planet

reasons.compensation: 30% of net profit rising to 50%, explicitly uncapped; scored below a straight percentage-of-sale rate because the base is net profit, not booking value.
reasons.contact_access: Published partnerships email (hello@campervanplanet.com) on the official affiliate page.
reasons.credibility: Operating booking platform with worldwide supplier coverage and published phone contacts, but a smaller name than the major travel networks.
reasons.niche_fit: Campervan and road-trip content is a strong, visual fit for travel creators, and the program is worldwide.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free signup in about a minute; affiliate code activated within 48 hours.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Creator tooling is unusually concrete (per-post source labels, widgets, banners), but no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

description: Single-product fashion accessory brand selling a $19.99 rubber shirt-stay belt that keeps shirts tucked in all day. Its affiliate program, powered by Endorsely, is built for short-form video creators and pays 25% commission per sale with no sales cap, instant links and no minimum followers.

evidence.summary: Official page states '25% Commission - You earn 25% on every sale ($5 per sale)... no cap, no tiers', a 'No Sales Cap' (infinity) badge, and the FAQ answers: 'There is no cap on how many sales you can make or how much you can earn.' 30-day cookie, $20 payout minimum, monthly payouts by PayPal or bank transfer.

Program is designed for TikTok, Reels and Shorts creators: no minimum followers, link issued instantly, video playbooks and hooks library, free product for creators with 5,000+ followers or after the first sale, plus a 20% audience discount code.
Scale signals on the official page: the brand claims 10,000+ users and its Amazon listing shows a 4.4 rating from 32 ratings - a small, young brand.

name: Shirt Tucker

reasons.compensation: 25% per sale ($5 on the $19.99 product) with explicit no-cap wording in the hero terms and FAQ - one of the clearest uncapped statements found this round.
reasons.contact_access: No email or contact is published on the page; joining runs through the Endorsely signup link.
reasons.credibility: Small single-product brand; its own page claims 10,000+ users but the linked Amazon listing has only 32 ratings.
reasons.niche_fit: A single, demonstrable wardrobe-fix product at $19.99 - narrow but very easy for fashion and workwear creators to show on camera.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Instant link on signup, no minimum followers, no approval step described.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The official page is written for short-form video creators, with playbooks, hooks and free-product rules; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

description: Ground and sea transportation booking platform with over 60,000 routes across more than 110 countries (buses, trains, ferries). Its own affiliate program pays 5% of the revenue share of each booking, with real-time reporting, monthly payments and a personal account manager, and advertises unlimited earning potential.

evidence.summary: Official page: 'With an unlimited earning potential, get paid for each successful reservation made using your affiliate link', and commission is stated as 'Get 5% of the revenue share of each booking made through your affiliate link' - the brand's own wording is a share of revenue, not 5% of the full booking price.

Program terms on the official page: 30-day attribution cookies, payment once commissions reach $50, monthly payments, wire transfer or PayPal, W-9/W-8BEN uploaded to the platform, and a personal account manager for affiliates.
Company details printed on the affiliate page for invoicing: Bookaway LTD, HaTa'as St 6, Ramat Gan 5251247, Israel.

name: Bookaway

reasons.compensation: Unlimited earning potential is stated, but the rate is 5% of the revenue share of a booking rather than of the booking price, so the effective take is modest and the wording is ambiguous.
reasons.contact_access: A personal account manager is promised after signup, but no direct email is published on the page.
reasons.credibility: Established travel-tech platform (60k+ routes, 24-hour support) with full company invoicing details printed on the page.
reasons.niche_fit: Ground transport in 110+ countries fits almost any travel itinerary content, especially Asia and Latin America routes.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free signup on the official page, subject to team approval.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The page explicitly invites travel websites, blogs and popular social media pages; no creator counts are published, so saturation stays unknown.

description: Onward-ticket proof service for visas and border checks, issuing real, verifiable airline PNRs. Its own affiliate program pays 25% commission on every referred sale with a 60-day cookie, monthly payouts, and a personal 10%-off code for the affiliate's audience, and its FAQ states there is no cap on earnings.

evidence.summary: Official FAQ: 'You earn 25% of what the customer pays on every booking made through your referral link or with your personal discount code. There's no cap - the more you refer, the more you earn.' Commissions become payable 30 days after the order; monthly payouts at a $50 minimum via PayPal or bank transfer; 60-day attribution.

Program is pitched at travel bloggers, digital-nomad communities, visa consultants, travel agencies, YouTubers and creators; every affiliate gets a personal 10%-off audience code that credits sales even without a link click; applications are reviewed by hand with a reply usually within 1 business day.

name: ProofofOnward

reasons.compensation: 25% of the customer price on every sale with an explicit 'There's no cap' FAQ answer - a high rate for travel services.
reasons.contact_access: No email is published on the page; contact is via the application form.
reasons.credibility: The product is verifiable-PNR based and the page is transparent about rules and prohibited promotion, but the brand is small and niche.
reasons.niche_fit: A narrow but real need - proof of onward travel for visas and border checks - that maps directly onto nomad, backpacker and expat content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free application with manual review, usually answered within 1 business day.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The page names creators and YouTubers as target partners and supports video/podcast attribution via personal codes; no creator counts published, so saturation stays unknown.

description: Marketplace where creators sell curated travel itineraries. Its own affiliate program pays 20% on standard trips (10% on founding-creator trips) with a 30-day cookie and Stripe payouts, no minimum audience, and an explicit no-earning-cap policy. The program is brand new - its own page showed zero active affiliates and zero sales at research time.

evidence.summary: Official page: 'No earning cap - promote unlimited trips to unlimited people', and the FAQ answers 'How much can I earn?' with 'No cap - the more you share, the more you earn.' Rates: 20% on standard trips, 10% on founding-creator trips; 30-day cookie; Stripe payouts.

Saturation evidence from the brand's own live counters on the affiliate page at research time: 0 active affiliates, 3 total clicks, 0 sales generated and $0 paid out - a brand-new, effectively empty program.

Open to anyone ('No minimum audience size... whether you have 100 or 100,000 followers'); free 30-second signup, unique links per trip, marketing assets provided, links work across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, blogs and email.

name: iliTrip

reasons.compensation: 20% on standard trips (10% on founding-creator trips) with explicit no-cap wording in the terms block and FAQ.
reasons.contact_access: No email or named contact is published on the page; signup is self-serve.
reasons.credibility: Credibility is low for now: the brand's own page shows 0 sales generated and $0 paid out, so the marketplace has no proven transaction volume yet.
reasons.niche_fit: Affiliates promote itineraries made by travel creators, so the product itself is creator content - a natural fit for travel UGC.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free, instant signup with no minimum audience.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Program is creator-first (per-trip links, assets, no audience minimum) and its own counters show zero active affiliates, which supports a low-saturation mark.

description: AI workout-plan app that builds personalised training and nutrition plans. Its own affiliate program pays 20% of net revenue on each referred plan purchase, recurring for as long as the referral keeps paying, with no approval step and Stripe payouts. The site's own footer states it is an independent AI tool and is not affiliated with Arnold Schwarzenegger.

evidence.summary: Official page: affiliates earn 20% of net revenue (after Stripe/Apple fees) on each plan purchase by a referred user, recurring while the referral keeps paying; terms list 'No cap' and 'No cap on earnings', and the FAQ answers 'Is there a cap on how much I can earn?' with 'There is no cap.'
Joining terms on the official page: no approval process - sign up for a free account, copy the referral link from the dashboard and share it; payouts via Stripe; worldwide.
Credibility caveat printed in the site's own footer: 'Arnold Training App is an independent AI tool and is not affiliated with Arnold Schwarzenegger.'

name: Arnold Training App

reasons.compensation: 20% of net revenue per referred plan, recurring while the referral pays, with an explicit 'There is no cap' FAQ answer; scored below gross-revenue rates because the base is net of platform fees.
reasons.contact_access: No email or contact is published on the page; everything runs through the app dashboard.
reasons.credibility: The site itself discloses it is an independent AI tool not affiliated with Arnold Schwarzenegger, so the famous name must not be read as an endorsement; scored low on credibility.
reasons.niche_fit: A workout-plan app is an easy fit for fitness creators' programming and transformation content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: No approval step - the link is issued on free-account signup.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Self-serve creator link with dashboard tracking, but the page shows no creator community, assets or counts, so saturation stays unknown.

description: London-based luxury modest-fashion and bridal label (Khanum's Ltd) recruiting fashion-forward content creators as affiliates. Creators join through the brand's LTK network and receive 10% on every order, with the brand stating there is no cap on commissions.

evidence.summary: Official affiliate page: 'Receive 10% on every order you generate' and, under 'No Limits on Earnings', 'The more you share, the more you earn, there's no cap on commissions.' Joining is via the page's 'JOIN OUR LTK NETWORK' button (creator.shopltk.com).

The page recruits 'fashion-forward content creators' and lists content formats it wants: styling reels, try-on hauls, modest styling tips, bridal features and behind-the-scenes content; affiliates get a unique tracking link/code and monthly payouts.
Beacons' brand directory lists 29 creators who have posted for Khanum's all time - a small absolute creator count that supports a low-saturation mark.
Trustpilot company details list Khanum's Ltd at E1, London, United Kingdom, describing it as a British Bangladeshi brand creating timeless investment pieces.

name: Khanum's

reasons.compensation: 10% on every order with explicit 'no cap on commissions' wording on the official page; a standard rate, lifted by the uncapped term.
reasons.contact_access: No email is published on the affiliate page; application runs through LTK.
reasons.credibility: A real London label (Khanum's Ltd) with press and retail presence, but a small affiliate operation run through LTK.
reasons.niche_fit: Luxury modest fashion and bridal is a defined, underserved creator niche with strong occasionwear content angles.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application via the LTK network button on the official page.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand names the exact UGC formats it wants (styling reels, try-on hauls, bridal features) and Beacons shows only 29 creators have ever posted for it, supporting low saturation.

description: Beach-lifestyle brand selling coordinated beach essentials and accessories. It runs both an affiliate program and a brand ambassador program for creators: affiliates earn a percentage on every sale with monthly payments and no cap on earnings, though the percentage itself is not published; ambassadors also receive free products and promo codes.

evidence.summary: Official page: 'Earn commissions: Earn a percentage on every sale generated from your link. Payments are made monthly, and there's no cap on how much you can earn!'
The percentage rate itself is not published anywhere on the official page - it is described only as 'competitive commission rates' - so commission_rate is recorded as null rather than guessed.

Ambassador track on the same page: free products, exclusive discounts and personalised promo codes, co-branded content and sponsored-post opportunities; open to creators, bloggers and influencers of any size who post beach, lifestyle and fashion content.

name: Baja Beach Co

opportunity.title: Baja Beach Co Affiliate & Ambassador Program

reasons.compensation: Uncapped earnings are stated explicitly, but the commission percentage is not published anywhere on the page, so compensation scores low until the rate is confirmed at application.
reasons.contact_access: No email is published on the page; questions go through the site's contact form.
reasons.credibility: Operating storefront with a defined two-track creator program, but a small brand with unpublished commercial terms.
reasons.niche_fit: Beach essentials and accessories fit summer, travel and lifestyle fashion content well.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application form on the official page, reviewed by the team.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Both an affiliate program and a content-focused ambassador program (free product, co-branded content, sponsored posts); no creator counts published, so saturation stays unknown.
